analysis.title: Prime Hedge Fund updates: Asia Fundamental L/S MTD Drawdown reaches -9.3% as Tech Route Deepens
key_insights: Asia Fundamental L/S hedge funds lost 2.2% on Oct 22 as the global tech sell-off deepened. Month-to-date drawdown is -9.3% and YTD return is 14.2%.
The drawdown from the June peak of 40% is now more than 25%. Median YTD performance is in the low single digits, so dispersion across managers is wide.
Beta and asset selection alpha are the main drivers of the MTD drawdown, followed by volatility and medium-term momentum factor effects.
Global Fundamental L/S managers fell 1.4% on Oct 22, are down 3.8% MTD and are up 8.8% YTD. Global Systematic L/S managers fell 1.3% on the day and are still up 19% YTD.
After heavy selling the prior week, Asia flows turned up week to date through Wednesday Oct 21, with short covers exceeding long sales 1.9 to 1.
Week-to-date buying was led by Korea (short covers), Hong Kong (long buys) and Taiwan (short covers). China saw selling, with long sales exceeding short covers.
China led week-to-date de-grossing (A-shares), followed by Korea and Taiwan. Hong Kong and Japan saw risk-on flows.
The region remains net sold month to date, led by Taiwan, Korea, Japan and China. Australia and Hong Kong saw net buying. Short sales exceeded long sales, so flows were marginally risk-on.
Info Tech dominated the net selling, with smaller contributions from Industrials and Financials.
Net allocation to Asia is down 295 bps MTD to 27.25%, a 10.8% overweight versus MSCI World AC. Gross allocation is down 141 bps MTD to 24.4%, a 7.9% overweight versus the benchmark.
China net and gross allocations are near 1-year lows, with net at 6.9% (7th percentile 1-year, 12th percentile 5-year) and gross at 6.5%.
Taiwan allocations remain high versus 5-year history, with net at 6.4% (92nd percentile 5-year) and gross at 4.3% (96th percentile 5-year).
risk_factors: The global tech sell-off is spreading into hedge fund performance across strategies and regions.
Asia allocations remain well above benchmark weights, which leaves room for further de-grossing if the sell-off continues.
Taiwan and Korea allocations are still high versus 5-year history.
